This is the most critical assumption because database compatibility is often the hardest constraint in API versioning. If v1 and v2 have incompatible schema requirements or write conflicting data, running them in parallel will cause data corruption or failures. Options A, B, and D are valid concerns but less critical - team capacity can be managed, client migration timing is flexible, and testing can happen before deployment. Database incompatibility is a hard blocker that can break both versions.
